' or the '

' token - in roughly positions 1-6, the break that ends a short opening line such as 'Solomon

', 'Meta

', and active-weak (0.25-0.5 of max) on most other tokens of a text's first two or three positions, including the first word of the body after the break. Deeper in the text its attention spreads over many token values and the strength falls (a break carrying the same content reads about 2.2 at position 15, 1.9 at 24, 1.3 at 33 and 0.6 at 80, i.e. 0.35, 0.31, 0.21 and 0.09 of max, and ordinary words are below the line past about 10 positions), so mid-text paragraph breaks, section headers, ordinary prose and code deep in a text are inactive, and a text made only of a comma-separated list of plain numbers ('3, 7, 12, 45') stays inactive too.

rival_explanations: Line-break detector at any depth: it fires on a '\n' token wherever the break falls, so a mid-document paragraph break or a section header deep in a text should be as active as a document-opening title.

Title-boundary head: it fires only on the line break that ends a short title-like line of 1-5 tokens and is quiet on ordinary early prose, so a text that opens with plain words and no line break (e.g. 'The committee met on Tuesday afternoon...') should be inactive.

Pure first-position head: its activity is just the excluded position-0 write bleeding into the next token, so replacing an opening line break with a period at the same position should leave the peak unchanged.
